title: Make git diff see a file it has never met
summary: New files are invisible to git diff and to hunk-level staging. `git add -N` registers the path without its content, which unlocks both — and quietly changes what `git stash` and `commit -a` will do.
mental_model: `add -N` puts the path in the index with empty content. Git now knows the file exists, so a diff against it shows every line as an addition — which is exactly what you need to review or partially stage a new file.

steps.title: Watch git diff ignore a whole file
steps.why: chemistry.py is untracked, so there is nothing in the index to compare it with. `git diff` reports nothing at all — which is why a new file can slip through a pre-commit review completely unseen.
steps.expect: Status lists it as ??, but diff is silent.

steps.title: Register the path without the content
steps.why: `-N` (or `--intent-to-add`) adds the path to the index pointing at an empty blob. You have told git the file is coming, without staging anything to commit.
steps.expect: It stops being ?? and becomes an index entry pointing at e69de29 — the hash of empty content, which every git repository contains.

verify.label: the path is in the index, pointing at the empty blob

steps.title: Now diff can see it
steps.why: Every line shows as an addition against the empty blob. This is the state that lets you review a new file with the same tools you use for edits.

steps.title: Stage only part of the new file
steps.why: This is the real payoff: hunk-level staging works on new files once they are intent-to-add. Here we stage the useful half and leave the debug helper out, using a patch — which is what `git add -p` does interactively.

write.content:
--- a/chemistry.py
+++ b/chemistry.py
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+PH_TARGET = 8.1
+
+
+def adjust(current):
+    return PH_TARGET - current

steps.expect: Staged: the constant and adjust(). Unstaged: the debug_dump helper you did not want yet.

steps.title: Commit the partial file
steps.why: The commit contains a five-line chemistry.py. The rest is still on disk, unstaged — a perfectly normal state that would have been impossible without -N.

verify.label: the committed file is the partial version

steps.title: Tidy up
steps.why: Commit the remainder, or drop it. Either way, notice you never had to choose between committing a whole new file and committing none of it.

verify.label: the new file arrived as two reviewable commits
verify.hint: add -N, stage one hunk, commit, then commit the rest

verify.label: the first commit holds only the reviewed half
the second commit adds the rest

pitfalls: An intent-to-add file makes `git stash` refuse in older git versions, and changes what `git commit -a` picks up. Do not leave files in this state.
`git commit` with only intent-to-add entries commits an empty file — the path with no content. Always check `git diff --staged` first.
Status shows an intent-to-add file as ` A` on modern git and `AM` on older versions. Either way it has stopped being `??`, which is your signal that -N is in play.
`git add -A` on an intent-to-add file stages it fully, discarding your careful partial selection.
cheatsheet: register the path, stage no content
now shows new files as all-additions
hunk-stage a new file, once -N is done
see the index entry and its blob hash
